summary.headline: MTAR Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR406.8 crore (+200% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 24.4%, while management held FY27 guidance of ~80% growth and 24% margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 200% YoY and 12.8% QoQ to INR406.8 crore, with EBITDA of INR99.2 crore (24.4% margin) and PAT of INR59.8 crore (14.7% margin). H1 FY27 operating cash flow was INR350 crore versus INR39.8 crore in H1 FY26, and working capital days fell to 50 from 172 in March 2026. H1 order inflows were a stated record INR4,102 crore, with closing order book of INR820 crore for civil nuclear cited. Management said H2 will be stronger than H1 but declined to raise guidance mid-year, saying it expects to land at the higher end of its guidance.

financial_highlights.value: Debt INR465 crore (LT INR189 crore, ST INR276 crore); investments INR358 crore; net debt about INR107 crore

segments.name: Civil nuclear
segments.commentary: Closing order book of INR820 crore supported by Kaiga and Gorakhpur orders and refurbishment programmes; Q2 nuclear order inflow of INR134 crore is refurbishment work with a 2-year execution period. Major revenue expected from FY28 to FY30, with some revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Clean energy – fuel cells (Bloom Energy hot boxes)
segments.commentary: Phase 2 capacity adds about 30% over existing capacity, expected operational by end-November 2026. Phase 3 multi-fold expansion in a new facility targeted for completion by June 2028.

segments.name: Product division (incl. ball screws, roller screws, box builds)
segments.commentary: Q2 product revenue reported at about INR126 crore after a reclassification of about INR60 crore from clean energy; management guided FY27 product revenue of close to INR500 crore. Ball screw exports commenced this quarter.

segments.name: MNC Aerospace
segments.commentary: Management aims for INR150 crore-plus MNC Aerospace revenue in FY27; first-article qualification for one key customer expected by year-end, with volume deliveries under long-term agreement from FY28. NADCAP-approved special process facility in place.

segments.name: Data center infrastructure (within clean energy)
segments.commentary: First-article orders worth about INR45 crore under execution; Phase 1 facility due end-November/early December 2026 and full facility by end-March 2027. Potential scale-up to INR350-450 crore over 2 years, per management.

segments.name: Oil and gas
segments.commentary: Dedicated facility expected operational by end-November 2026; development and first-article qualification completed with Weatherford, other first articles in progress. Meaningful ramp from FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged at about 80% revenue growth and 24% EBITDA margin; management said it expects to perform at the higher side but would not revise guidance mid-year.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, supported by order book and execution; management expects a strong closing order book at end-FY27.
Working capital days targeted at about 100 by end-FY27 and about 150 days as long-term goal over 2-3 years; GST refunds of INR70-80 crore per year expected.
ROCE expected to improve to about 23% by end-FY27 from 17.2% in FY26.

Total capex planned about INR500 crore (INR350 crore fuel cells, INR150 crore other verticals), 75% debt and 25% internal accruals; about INR400 crore of this to be spent in FY27 on top of about INR100 crore in FY26.
Civil nuclear to target 100 GW by 2047 per government; Mahi Banswara private 700 MW reactor bids could be worth INR700-1,000 crore per management.

qa_highlights.question: Fuel cell hot box capacity after Phase 2 and order outlook from Bloom over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 is about 30% above existing capacity; multi-fold Phase 3 due by June 2028; management said demand exceeds what it can supply and orders are continuous.

qa_highlights.question: Total capex including Phase 2 and 3 and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Total about INR500 crore (INR350 crore fuel cells, INR150 crore other verticals), 75% debt and 25% internal accruals; debt currently INR189 crore long-term.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin expand in H2 or stay near 24%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects improvement and to land at the higher end of 80% growth and 24% margin guidance, but will not change guidance mid-year.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of working capital improvement and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Target about 100 days by end-FY27 and about 150 days long term over 2-3 years; GST refunds of INR70-80 crore a year and better advances cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why did product division revenue fall QoQ, and what is its run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crore was misclassified under clean energy; corrected Q2 product revenue is about INR126 crore, with FY27 guidance close to INR500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear revenue timing for Kaiga 6 and the Q2 nuclear order?
qa_highlights.answer: Some revenue in FY27, majority from FY28 to FY30; the INR134 crore Q2 nuclear order is refurbishment work with a 2-year execution.

qa_highlights.question: Was the revenue growth guidance raised given inventory and H2 ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on 100-120% growth scenarios and reiterated it will do better than the 80% guidance.

capex_capacity: Total capex planned about INR500 crore: INR350 crore for fuel cells and INR150 crore for other verticals such as oil and gas and aerospace; 75% debt-funded and 25% internal accruals.
CFO: INR500 crore capex spend is roughly INR100 crore in FY26 plus INR400 crore in FY27; sustenance and growth capex of INR50-100 crore a year thereafter for 1-2 years.
Fuel cells: Phase 2 adds about 30% over existing hot box capacity, operational by end-November 2026; Phase 3 multi-fold expansion in a new dedicated facility targeted for June 2028.
Data center: Phase 1 facility due end-November or early December 2026; Phase 2 by June 2027 per call (CEO also said full facility by end-March 2027 in prepared remarks).
Oil and gas dedicated facility expected operational by end-November 2026; meaningful ramp from FY28.
Civil nuclear: no major capex needed beyond bottleneck areas; major facility to be planned after observing demand over the next year. Company evaluating greenfield aerospace facilities.
demand_pricing: Record H1 FY27 order inflow of INR4,102 crore (figure partly inaudible on transcript); management expects strong closing order book at end-FY27.

Civil nuclear: closing order book INR820 crore; Q2 nuclear order inflow INR134 crore is refurbishment work with a 2-year execution; major revenue FY28-FY30, some revenue in FY27. Mahi Banswara (4 x 700 MW private reactors) could be worth INR700-1,000 crore.

Product division: Q2 revenue about INR126 crore after roughly INR60 crore reclassified from clean energy (box builds); FY27 guidance close to INR500 crore; orders are short-cycle, within about 1 year. Ball screw exports commenced.

MNC Aerospace: aspiring to INR150 crore-plus revenue in FY27; works with 4 customers; electromechanical actuator opportunity about INR150 crore with no fixed timeline; AMCA and LCA Tejas volume orders expected later.
Data center: first-article orders about INR45 crore; potential scale-up to INR350-450 crore over 2 years, with management citing customer indication of roughly 8x the first-article value.
Advances: civil nuclear tender terms about 30-40% advance; other customers 20% or future-deliverable advances. Only about USD1 million of receivables discounted.
Competition: management said no other supplier of hot boxes besides MTAR and one South Korean company; Bloom took 12-15 years to develop; forex gain INR2.3 crore of INR8.5 crore other income in Q2.
risks_watch: Guidance held at ~80% revenue growth despite H1 run-rate; management declined to update, so H2 delivery vs implied run-rate is the key test.
Product division figures were restated by about INR60 crore for classification; watch whether reported segment numbers match the corrected presentation.
Working capital days expected to rise to about 100 by end-FY27 from 50 as volumes grow; advances are negotiated customer by customer.
Execution timelines: Phase 2 fuel cell capacity (end-Nov 2026), oil and gas facility (end-Nov 2026), and data center Phase 1 (end-Nov/early Dec 2026) must be met.
Concentration risk: fuel cell growth tied to Bloom Energy; management said AI capex slowdown concerns were speculation.

Aerospace and defense volume ramp depends on first-article qualifications by year-end and long-term agreement volumes from FY28; several large targets (INR600-700 crore defense and aerospace by FY30) lack disclosed capex or LOA backing.
key_quotes: We have a closing order book of INR820 crores, supported by order inflows from Kaiga and Gorakhpur and also from the refurbishment programs.

Yes, there was a small error in that. There was almost INR60 crores of classification done in other segment, which was supposed to go into the product division, which they are correcting it right now.
But definitely, we are confident that we'll be on the higher side in terms of the guidance what we have given.
So we are working towards all this and all this are on track as far as we are concerned.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book, execution timelines and margins, but deliberately cautious on guidance: management repeatedly declined to raise FY27 guidance mid-year and was evasive on asset turnover, sector-wise capital intensity and specific order-inflow timing, citing NDAs and time constraints.

Fuel cell Phase 3 multi-fold expansion in new dedicated facility, targeted June 2028
Data centre Phase 1 facility (end-Nov/early Dec 2026); full facility by end-March 2027
Oil and gas dedicated facility, operational by end-November 2026

growth.why: FY27 guidance of ~80% revenue growth and 24% EBITDA margin held, with management expecting the higher end; backing is partial: a record H1 order inflow of INR4,102 crore and a civil nuclear order book of INR820 crore, plus fuel cell Phase 2 (~30% capacity add) due by end-November 2026, but no specific FY27 revenue bridge was given.
